blocks.text: Organizing your procurement inbox on Mac

Procurement officers often deal with over 100 emails per day. You need a system that keeps your inbox clear. Start by using the [create a folder in Outlook](/how-to/create-a-folder-in-outlook) feature. Create folders for each major supplier or project phase. This keeps your main inbox focused on urgent tasks.

Rules are your best friend for automation. Use the [create a rule in Outlook](/how-to/create-a-rule-in-outlook) tool to move emails from specific vendors directly into their respective folders. This prevents your inbox from becoming a bottleneck. You can also set rules to flag emails from your manager or key internal stakeholders.

Speed matters when you have a long list of purchase orders to process. Use ⌘ + 1 to jump to your Mail view. Use ⌘ + 2 for your Calendar. These shortcuts save seconds that add up over the day. If you need to search for a specific invoice number, use ⌥ + ⌘ + F to focus the search bar immediately.

Microsoft does not provide a custom shortcut menu in the app. You must set custom shortcuts in System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > App Shortcuts. Enter the exact menu command name to map your preferred keys. This is helpful for actions you perform hundreds of times per week.

Negotiations happen over email. Keep your replies professional and clear. Use the [create an email signature in Outlook](/how-to/create-an-email-signature-in-outlook) feature to include your contact details and procurement policy links. This reduces the number of follow up questions you receive.

If you are waiting for a quote, use the [set a reminder for an email in Outlook](/how-to/set-a-reminder-for-an-email-in-outlook) feature. This helps you track vendor responsiveness without manual spreadsheets. You can also [delay delivery of an email in Outlook](/how-to/delay-delivery-of-an-email-in-outlook) to ensure your messages arrive at the start of the next business day.

Your ERP system is central to your role. Do not treat Outlook as a separate island. When you receive a purchase requisition, immediately create a calendar event using the [create a calendar event in Outlook](/how-to/create-a-calendar-event-in-outlook) tool. This links the deadline to your workflow.

If you use a shared mailbox for team inquiries, use the [add a shared mailbox in Outlook](/how-to/add-a-shared-mailbox-in-outlook) guide to keep everything in one place. This ensures no vendor request goes unanswered. Always check if your procurement software provides an Outlook add-in to sync data directly.

items: Leaving all emails in the inbox instead of using folders.
Relying on memory to track vendor quotes instead of using flags or reminders.
Ignoring the New Outlook transition, which is required for modern Exchange features.
Forgetting to check the Focused Inbox settings, which might hide important vendor mail.
Manually copying data between Outlook and your ERP instead of using export tools.

blocks.text: Transitioning to the New Outlook is necessary. The legacy version will lose support for Exchange Online in October 2026. Start moving your archives now to avoid data loss. Use the [import an OLM file in Outlook](/how-to/import-an-olm-file-in-outlook) feature if you need to migrate old data from the legacy version.

faq.question: How can I find emails faster in Outlook for Mac?
faq.answer: Use the [search with filters in Outlook](/how-to/search-with-filters-in-outlook) feature. You can filter by sender, date, or attachments to narrow down results quickly.

faq.question: Can I use custom keyboard shortcuts in Outlook?
faq.answer: Yes. You can assign them via System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > App Shortcuts on your Mac.

faq.question: Is the legacy version of Outlook still safe to use?
faq.answer: Microsoft is retiring legacy support for Exchange Online in October 2026. You should switch to the New Outlook now.

faq.question: How do I handle too many emails from one supplier?
faq.answer: Use the [create a rule in Outlook](/how-to/create-a-rule-in-outlook) feature to automatically move their emails into a dedicated folder.
